newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney's socialites preen for Princess Di.
newsitem.headline: Sydney's socialites preen for Princess Di.

text.p: Princess Diana, Britain's self-styled Queen of Hearts, will visit Australia this week for a fund-raising trip that has forced the socialites of Sydney to dig out their manuals on etiquette.
Since her divorce from Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, two months ago, Diana is no longer a royal. Curtseys are out and plain "princess" will replace "your Royal Highness".
But in egalitarian Australia, where even the prime minister is addressed as "mate", being an ex-royal carries no stigma -- and Diana is proving as big a draw as ever.

In fact the big topic of conversation in Sydney's social circles is who will dance with Diana at her main dinner engagement, with most tipping bachelor James Packer, son of Australia's richest man and media boss Kerry Packer.

Organisers of the princess's visit to Sydney say more than 900 people have paid A$1,000 (US$590 each) to hear her speak at the dinner on Thursday to raise money for the city's Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute.
And newspapers have been advising readers where to go to catch a glimpse of the world's most photographed princess as she turns up for each glitzy engagement.
Up to 200 members of the British press pack, never tiring of a good royal story, are expected to follow Diana Down Under. Organisers say 150 photographers are accredited for her visit.
Much of the visit, which starts on Thursday and ends on Monday, will be private.

After Thursday's dinner, Diana visits the Chang institute and a hospital on Friday morning before a fund-raising lunch for homeless children. On Saturday, she will pay a private visit to a Sydney hospice. The rest of the time she is expected to relax.
It will be Diana's first trip to Australia since she came, with her former husband, for the country's 1988 bicentenary.

During that trip she enjoyed the fanfare of a full-scale royal tour. This time around she will be offered top-class corporate hospitality, including a sponsored limousine from a Japanese car -- with her favourite Elton John CDs.

But she could face some rare competition in the glamour stakes. Organiser Emma Cooper said plans to put Diana in the top suite at a deluxe Sydney hotel were foiled because American soap siren Priscilla Presley had already booked it.
Organisers refuse to say where Diana will be staying instead.
Also in town this week, publicising books on the chat show circuit, are British actress Joan Collins and veteran Hollywood dancer Cyd Charisse.
